proofs.title: Schmidt-rank obstruction
proofs.summary: The anticoherent reduction must have full rank in its symmetric subspace; the complementary subsystem must be large enough to accommodate the same Schmidt spectrum.
proofs.bodyHtml: The two complementary reductions have the same nonzero Schmidt spectrum. Anticoherence requires \rho_t=I_{t+1}/(t+1), of rank t+1. The complement is supported on \operatorname{Sym}^{n-t}(\mathbb C^2), of dimension n-t+1. Hence t+1\le n-t+1.

proofs.title: Odd-size complement obstruction
proofs.summary: A one-dimensional complementary kernel would itself have an impossible Schmidt rank.
proofs.bodyHtml:
If \rho_t=I_{t+1}/(t+1), its complement \rho_{t+1} has t+1 equal nonzero eigenvalues in a symmetric space of dimension t+2. Thus \rho_{t+1}=(I_{t+2}-|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|)/(t+1) for a normalized symmetric (t+1)-qubit vector |\phi\rangle.

Trace one qubit, using \operatorname{Tr}_1 I_{\mathrm{sym}}^{(t+1)}=\frac{t+2}{t+1}I_{\mathrm{sym}}^{(t)}. Comparing with \rho_t yields \rho_t^\phi=I_{t+1}/(t+1). But \rho_t^\phi has rank at most two because |\phi\rangle has a single-qubit complement. This contradicts t+1\ge3.

references.location: Schmidt-rank framework; the odd-complement deduction is newly supplied by the catalogue

proofs.title: Spin-tensor Gram obstruction
proofs.summary: The spin-tensor Gram matrix gives a quadratic necessary condition on the number of qubits.
proofs.bodyHtml:
Put q=\lfloor t/2\rfloor. For Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal tensors A,B of ranks at most q, the product A^\dagger B has ranks at most 2q\le t. Anticoherence therefore gives \langle\psi|A^\dagger B|\psi\rangle=\operatorname{Tr}(A^\dagger B)/(n+1).

The (q+1)^2 vectors A|\psi\rangle consequently have a positive diagonal Gram matrix, so they are linearly independent in the (n+1)-dimensional spin space.

proofs.title: Eight qubits cannot be fourth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact two-copy identity would give a negative total-spin probability if all multipoles through rank four vanished.
proofs.bodyHtml: Here p_J is the total-spin-J probability of two copies, and a_L is the nonnegative squared length of rank-L spin multipoles. Fourth-order anticoherence sets a_1,\ldots,a_4 to zero, forcing p_0=-4/27, a contradiction. The coefficient identity is checked with exact rational arithmetic.

references.location: Multipole/purity convention; this exclusion identity is an independent catalogue calculation

proofs.title: Nine qubits cannot be third-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact four-copy positivity certificate proves the previously reported exclusion for every pure symmetric nine-qubit state.

references.location: Sec. 4.4.3 reports absence; the exact proof is independently derived in this catalogue.

proofs.bodyHtml:
Average four copies of a hypothetical third-order anticoherent state over collective rotations. The resulting operator X is positive, has \operatorname{Tr}X=1, and obeys exact linear contraction equations from its vanishing rank-one, rank-two and rank-three multipoles.

In an explicit angular-momentum basis, eighty-five independent rational equations leave a three-dimensional space of candidates. Four diagonal coordinates obey a strictly positive linear relation summing to zero. Positivity forces all four coordinates to vanish; they determine the remaining three parameters, hence X=0. This contradicts \operatorname{Tr}X=1.

sourceCaveats: Order means at least t. Every t-AC state is also s-AC for s ≤ t; a witness does not prove that t is the largest possible order at that qubit number.
Full anticoherence requires every multipole rank 1,…,t to vanish. Cancelling only even multipoles, or attaining an even-sector lower bound, does not suffice.
The symmetric t-body identity has dimension t+1, not 2^t. These states are distinct from absolutely maximally entangled qubit states.
PRResearch 4, 013178 (2022), PDF p.17 Table IV labels a nine-qubit state order 3 although its rank-three multipole and reduced matrix are nonzero. Its verified order is 2.

The same 2022 table prints ten-qubit coefficients with squared norm 43/55. Replacing the two endpoint amplitudes 1/√11 by 1/√5 gives a normalized third-order state; this is an independently checked correction, not a published erratum.
Blank cells in the 2017 numerical survey mean failed convergence. Restricted cyclic-construction thresholds in the 2015 paper are not universal existence thresholds.

The eleven-qubit third-order representative with radical complex amplitudes is independently derived and exactly checked here; it is not attributed to the rounded numerical vector in the 2017 appendix.
definition: A pure symmetric N-qubit state is t-anticoherent iff rho_t is the maximally mixed state I_(t+1)/(t+1) on the symmetric t-qubit subspace. Equivalently all spin moments through order t are independent of direction. This requires every multipole rank1,...,t to vanish, not only the even ranks.
